newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index ends sharply up on leadership.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends sharply up on leadership.

text.p: Shenzhen B share index leaped up on Friday with investors increasingly confident over the stability of China's in the aftermath of Deng Xiaoping's death, brokers said.
The B share index rose 7.43 points or 5.18 percent to 150.96 on turnover of HK$127.19 million compared with HK$215 million on Thursday.
The A share index zigzagged up 8.68 points or 2.48 percent at 359.28 points, on turnover of 6.57 billion yuan compared with Thursday's 10.2 billion yuan.
Brokers said investors were also encouraged by sharp rises in Shanghai's A share market.
"The Shanghai stock market performed well because investors can see a smooth leadership transition taking place," an analyst at Central-South Securities said.
"The bad news has been digested and the B index seems likely to move steadily upwards over the next week," he said.
Shanghai's B index rose 0.894 points or 1.38 percent to 65.569 points and the A share index closed at a year high of 1063.276 points, rising 55.545 points or 5.51 percent.
As to the medium-term trend, analysts are mixed. "I think the market will continue to be volatile," said one.
Another analyst said that with the growing sense of political stability, stocks are poised to rise in the months before the Hong Kong handover in July.

Others were more cautious, saying they preferred to wait and see how things developed. On the B share market, floppy disk maker Shenzhen Benelux Enterprise Co Ltd was the best performer and gained HK$0.37 or 8.04 percent to HK$4.97 on volume of 167,740 shares.
Hefei Meilin Co Ltd, a refrigerator maker, rose HK$0.43 or 7.72 percent to HK$6.00 on volume of 2.70 million shares, making it most active counter of the day.

On the A share market, chemical fibre maker Baoding Swan Co, which floated 67.50 million A shares on Friday, ended the session at 13.88 yuan against an offer price of 6.30 yuan per share. Volume was a hefty 54.64 million shares.
